author: Parsifal-2045
body:
#### PR description:

While running a few measurements for https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52146 and https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52158 with the Phase-2 HLT menu, I've noticed a weird plateau on both CPU- and GPU-offloaded configurations. After some investigation and some help from Claude, I've found a few missing ROOT dictionaries that forced a fallback to `cling` and hit its global lock, significantly slowing down the processing. 

The existing dictionary checks do not catch these cases: they rely on `TClass::GetMissingDictionaries`, which stops recursing at container elements (and `pair`/`tuple` template arguments) that have a dictionary, so classes without dictionaries reached only through them go unnoticed.

This PR adds an `edm::LogWarning` (category `MissingDictionaries`), issued before the first event, listing such classes for each affected product type:

- `edm::findClassesWithoutDictionaries()` (`FWCore/Reflection`): a version of `TClass::GetMissingDictionaries` that also descends into those container elements and template arguments, and reports every class for which `TClass::HasDictionary()` is false (classes built by cling are `kInterpreted`, classes known only from the streamer info of a file are `kEmulated`).
- `edm::warnAboutMissingDictionaries()` (`FWCore/Framework`): issues the warning once per product type, and is called
  - when registering the branches of an input file (`RootTree::addBranch`, first commit), and
  - for every product kept by an output module (`OutputModuleCore::keepThisBranch`, second commit), which covers products made in the job.

For each class that does not have a dictionary defined, a warning like the following is printed before the first event starts processing

```
%MSG-w MissingDictionaries:  AfterFile 15-Oct-2026 20:44:15 CEST pre-events
No data dictionary found for the following classes, needed by product
'EcalEBTriggerPrimitiveDigisSorted_simEcalEBTriggerPrimitiveDigis__HLT.' of type 'edm::SortedCollection<io_v1::EcalEBTriggerPrimitiveDigi,edm::StrictWeakOrdering<io_v1::EcalEBTriggerPrimitiveDigi> >':

  std::vector<EcalEBTriggerPrimitiveSample>

ROOT falls back to the much slower interpreter (cling) or streamer emulation
for them. Add '<class name="..."/>' for each to the classes_def.xml of the
package that defines it (for a container, of its elements), with the header
in classes.h, or drop the product if it is not needed.
%MSG
```

Adding the reported dictionaries is left to follow-up PRs in the affected packages. In a typical Phase-2 HLT workflow (with validation), the warnings report:

| Product | Classes without a dictionary |
|---|---|
| `EcalEBTriggerPrimitiveDigisSorted_simEcalEBTriggerPrimitiveDigis__HLT` | `std::vector<EcalEBTriggerPrimitiveSample>` |
| `l1tPFClusters_l1tLayer1Barrel_DecodedEmClusters_HLT` | `std::vector<std::pair<edm::Ptr<l1t::io_v1::L1Candidate>,float> >` |
| `l1tPFJets_l1tSC4PFL1PuppiCorrectedEmulator__HLT` | `edm::Ptr<l1t::io_v1::PFCandidate>` and its vector, `l1ct::io_v1::JetTagClass` and its vector |
| `l1tTrackerMuons_l1tTkMuonsGmt__HLT` | `std::vector<edm::Ref<std::vector<l1t::io_v1::SAMuon>,...> >` |
| `TICLCandidates_hltTiclCandidate__HLTX` | `edm::Ptr<reco::io_v1::GsfTrack>`, `edm::Ptr<ticl::io_v1::Trackster>` and their vectors |
| `ticlTracksters_hltTiclCandidate__HLTX` | `std::vector<std::array<unsigned int,2> >` (`Trackster::edges_`) |

No change in the physics output is expected.

#### PR validation:

Code builds and unit tests pass.

Running  a workflow generated using the following recipe (on TTbar 200 PU files)
```bash
cmsDriver.py step2 -s L1P2GT,HLT:75e33,VALIDATION:@hltValidation \
    --datatier GEN-SIM-DIGI-RAW,DQMIO \
    --eventcontent FEVTDEBUGHLT,DQMIO \
    --conditions auto:phase2_realistic_T35 \
    -n 1000 \
    --geometry ExtendedRun4D121 \
    --era Phase2C22I13M9 \
    --filein $ALL_FILES \
    --process HLTX \
    --inputCommands='keep *, drop *_hlt*_*_HLT, drop triggerTriggerFilterObjectWithRefs_l1t*_*_HLT' \
    --python_filename gpu_config.py \
    --no_exec

```
The warnings match the state of every  `TClass` in ROOT at the end of the job (all reported cases finish with state `kInterpreted`).
No interpreted or emulated class used by a product read or written in the job goes unreported, except `pair` types (whose arguments are checked instead, as in `TClass::GetMissingDictionaries`) and ROOT/framework internals.

FYI @fwyzard
title: Add runtime warning for missing ROOT dictionaries for classess using containers
